q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
The data doesn't match the question's premise: ROAS is up and net profit is actually less negative (the loss narrowed). Net ROAS rose from 0.84x to 0.88x while net profit improved from a loss of ₹69,606 to a loss of ₹38,919 (period 2026-10-02..2026-10-08 → 2026-10-09..2026-10-15). This means ad efficiency improved even though top-line volumes fell.

What’s behind it
- Net ROAS rose because Contribution margin per order increased materially: contribution margin per order moved ~+25.2%, while ad‑spend per order rose ~+19.4% — the net effect raised ROAS (contribution up more than ad cost per order). ROAS: 0.8376 → 0.8783 (≈ +4.9%).
- Net profit moved toward break‑even because both ad spend and contribution fell, but contribution fell less in proportional terms than the drop in ad spend per the P&L bridge: net profit −₹69,606 → −₹38,919 (loss narrowed by 44.1%).
- Volumes collapsed: Orders fell 376 → 235 (−37.5%) and Net sales fell ₹7,00,185 → ₹4,52,760 (−35.3%). Ad spend also fell ₹4,28,544 → ₹3,19,685 (−25.4%). Lower orders mean smaller totals even as per-order economics improved.
- Mix effects drove the ROAS gain (Simpson‑style): some ad formats (SHOP_NOW) lost a larger share of volume, changing the weighted average ROAS even though many within-format rates moved differently.

Worth checking:
- Which campaigns / formats lost the most orders (SHOP_NOW had large volume drops) and whether that volume loss is profitable to recover — restoring volume could widen or shrink the ROAS depending on its contribution-per-order.

Period: 2026-10-02..2026-10-08 → 2026-10-09..2026-10-15 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-15
